## M2 — The reference family

The instance everything is tested against. It is **invented and tunable** — validation is against the theory's regularities, not against one family's history — so every value here is `[I]` and the whole of M11 carries the falsification burden.

**M2.1** The reference family **MUST** be declared in markdown config, not in source. → M0.3

**M2.2** It **MUST** span three generations and **MUST** include at least one cut-off tie and at least one family-of-origin tie per adult (M1.D.8).

**M2.3** Phase B **MUST** run on a reduced instance — the nuclear four of M2.A.0 **plus** their family-of-origin ties, even if those agents only hold a bond energy. A closed nuclear four **MUST NOT** be used, because it cannot compute its own driving term.

**M2.3a** — *the Phase B instance.* Members: Ravi, Marta, Nadia and Pia, active; Ana, Sofia and Bruno, holding bond energy and acting only by script. Ties: Ravi–Marta; Ravi–Nadia; Ravi–Pia; Marta–Nadia; Marta–Pia; Marta–Ana; Ravi–Sofia; Ana–Bruno, cut off. Ana–Bruno is the dormant family-of-origin tie on which Phase B's exit condition places its `TRIGGER`. `structural_importance` **MUST NOT** be declared in the Phase B instance, because `M1.A.13a` derives it.

**The life course.** Ages are computed from `M2.A.0j`'s settings; the children's level and chronic anxiety are their parents' mean at `t0` (`M7.E.1f`, `M7.B.1a`), which the run then derives; Dr Halim is female and 35. The Phase B and Phase C instances keep the values this table had before; they are the closed phases' records.

**The owner's reference family.** The owner's account of the family is: grandparents (4), parents (2), children (3), the parents' siblings (2), and the coach (1). Bruno (Ana's cut-off brother) and Toma (Iris's son) leave the table. Viktor (Sofia's husband, Ravi's father) and Dario (Ravi's brother, cut off from Ravi) join it. Their values are `[I]`, drafted for the owner's review. Ravi stays "eldest of 3"; the third sibling is not in the instance. The Phase B and Phase C instances (`M2.3a`, `config/bowen/family_phase_c.md`) are the closed phases' records and keep Bruno.

**M2.A.0** The instance declares **eleven family members plus one external agent**. "Twelve-person reference family" is loose shorthand: Dr Halim is `role = EXTERNAL` and **MUST NOT** be counted in family membership, in the tie matrix of M2.B.1, or in `positions_live` unless the live-position test of M8 admits him. The nuclear family for M2.3 is **Ravi, Marta, Nadia and Pia** — Leo is launched and is not part of the Phase B spike.

**M2.A.0a** `chronic_anxiety` for generations 1 and 2 **MUST** be supplied as an initial condition, because M1.A.7 and M7.B.1 fix it in childhood from witnessed history and those childhoods are never simulated. The test is **life stage, not generation**: an initial value **MUST** be supplied for every agent already past the fixation age at `t0`, and **MUST** be an error for any agent who is not. With the starting ages of `M2.A.0j`, Leo (9), Nadia (4) and Pia (1) are below the fixation age at `t0`. They carry no supplied value, and the derived path (`M7.B.1a`) applies to them as to children born in the run.

**M2.A.0b** There is **no calendar epoch**. All dates **MUST** be expressed as a duration relative to `t0`. `t0` is the starting point, week 0, and is not a slow tick; the first slow tick falls at the end of week 51. M3 defines only relative clocks, so a literal year has nothing to resolve against.

**M2.A.0c** Spouses **MUST** be paired at comparable **`basic_level`**, never `functional_level`. 1979 Tape 3 specifies the field: Bowen says that when spouses are said to match on differentiation, the base level is meant, not functioning, which shifts up and down easily. The KB14 interview gives the matching as one of the fairly constant facts from the family research — people choose spouses whose differentiation of self is nearly the same as their own — and as the usual case, including in couples who live together. → `kb/kb14.md` · K14.2; `theory/_LECTURES_1979.md` · B9

**M2.A.0e** — *the match is close, not exact.* *Ravi's `basic_level` was 38 against Marta's 40, outside this requirement's own tolerance (review C); changed to 39.* Pairing **MUST** use a declared **tolerance**, not equality: **±1 point** on the 0–100 scale, declared in config. → user amendment to D3, 2026-08-24
**Why a tolerance is the right shape.** The corpus's own claim is "**almost identical**", not identical, and Kerr adds that pairing is **strict for spouses and looser for friendships** — basic level "**also influence[s] the development of close friendships but somewhat less precisely**" (`kerr_book/ks07.md` · KS07.7). A wider tolerance therefore applies to non-family ties.
**And it is what makes `M11.C.24` observable**: the initial gap must be small enough that the *developed* divergence dominates it.

**M2.A.0f** Pairing **MUST** carry a second, orthogonal dimension: **rank and sex complementarity** of sibling position (M1.A.14). Complementary pairs form more readily and carry lower baseline conflict, and incompatible ones **MUST** be able to fail to form — "**if the female in this case was less deferential and the male is bothered by it, the relationship might not take.**" This affects **conflict propensity, not differentiation**: "**This does not mean that one marriage is more mature than the other.**" → `kerr_book/ks12.md` · KS12.3; `ks07.md` · KS07.9

**M2.A.0d** Fusion **MUST** be life-stage dependent, not uniformly costly. The infant–caretaker symbiosis is stated as a **normal state, not a pathology**. → `kb/kb14.md` · K14.5

**M2.A.0g** — *pole assignment **MUST** be independent of sex.* "**males and females assume the dominant position with equal frequency.**" `M1.B.5`'s dominant pole **MUST NOT** correlate with sex across an ensemble. This is a hard constraint a natural implementation could easily violate — any asymmetry in the assignment rule surfaces as a sex effect at readout — and it is assertable: see `M11.C.25`. → *decision A4-tail, 2026-08-27*; `theory/family_evaluation/fe07.md` · FE07.3

**M2.A.0h** The reference family's declaration **MUST** assign each member the fixed identifier `M1.A.20` requires. Display names **MUST NOT** serve as identifiers. → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C2

**M2.A.0i** — *the `Sex` column.* It carries `M1.A.21`'s field. Where the table's own relationship words fix a member's sex (mother, daughter, sister, brother, husband, son) the column states it; Ravi, Nadia and Pia were declared by the owner on 2026-10-06. **Leo and Dr Halim were not stated** at revision 13 and **MUST** be declared before Phase D, the first phase whose instance includes them. *Leo declared male by the owner, 2026-10-10. Dr Halim declared female by the owner, 2026-10-13 (revision 28, `M2.A.0k`); revision 34 records it here (MR-13).*

**M2.A.0j** — *starting ages are settings.* The owner (2026-10-13): starting ages are "1 for 3rd generation's youngest child, 30 for second, 55 for third [the grandparents]. Allow these as settings in app." The family config **MUST** declare three settings: `start_age_youngest_g3` (1), `start_age_g2` (30) and `start_age_g1` (55). Each person **MUST** declare an age gap to their generation's anchor: the youngest member for generation 3, the eldest for generations 2 and 1 (the owner named the youngest for generation 3; the eldest for the others is Claude's reading). Showing the settings in the run visualization app is deferred: this revision puts them in config, where the app can read them. The loader **MUST** compute each age from the anchor and the gap. Changing a setting **MUST NOT** change any other value. An external agent enters at `coach_start_age_years` (35, the owner's), and a member with no generation is an error.

### M2.B Ties `[I]`

**M2.B.1** Eleven family members give 55 possible pairs (Dr Halim is external and is not in this matrix — M2.A.0); the instance **MUST** declare only the ties that carry traffic, and **MUST NOT** instantiate the full matrix.

**M2.B.2** The declared set **MUST** include: the Ravi–Marta marriage; both parental ties to each of Leo, Nadia and Pia; Marta–Ana; Ravi–Sofia; Ravi–Viktor; Sofia–Viktor; Ravi–Dario (cut off); Marta–Iris (resolved, low contact); Ana–Teodor; and Dr Halim's tie to whichever member is being coached. The owner confirmed it: "Coach is tied to Coachee." The reference config's ties from Dr Halim to both spouses **MUST** change to one tie, to the member the coaching script names, at plan step L1. `M11.C.7`'s joint arm is a test arm, not the reference family, and declares a tie to each spouse.
